Kerala.scheme: PM-AJAY (Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana)
Kerala.component_analysed: Grants-in-Aid / 'Grant to States' component (former SCA-to-SCSP). The central rule-set is identical across states - see the Tamil Nadu pack for the full guideline analysis (pmajay.dosje.gov.in Guidelines July 2020 + AAP circular). This file adds the Kerala implementation layer.
Kerala.prose_summary: The national PM-AJAY skill rules apply unchanged in Kerala: no trade/QP whitelist exists; eligibility is by programme type (RPL 32-80h; short-term 200-600h or per QP/NOS; EDP 80h; long-term 6-12 months+), all training must be NSQF-compliant and within MSDE Common Cost Norms, with >=70% placement (wage or self-employment), >=30% women, and at least 10% of each yearly release spent on skill development. Kerala-specific findings from this pass: (1) The state implementation runs through the Directorate of Scheduled Caste Development (SCDD), Government of Kerala (scdd.kerala.gov.in); its Scheduled Caste Sub Plan 2022-23 plan document allocates Rs 4,900 lakh for 'training, employment and Human Resource Development', including 'finishing schools cum skill centres' in Model Residential Schools for residential coaching and employability in emerging sectors, area-specific livelihood programmes with the Industries/Agriculture/Animal-Husbandry departments, and Pre-Examination Training Centres (PETCs) in all districts. (2) A concrete PM-AJAY-funded programme in the state: Digital University Kerala (duk.ac.in), 'in partnership with the Directorate of Scheduled Caste Department', admits SC candidates to three one-year RESIDENTIAL skill programmes (Blockchain, Cyber Security, PCB Design) under PM-AJAY - a live example of the 'long-term course (6-12 months)' category being used, consistent with the central rule. (3) Kerala's SSDM counterpart is the Kerala Academy for Skills Excellence (KASE) and the Higher Education Department's ASAP Kerala (a Companies Act Section-8 state PSU), whose Community Skill Parks are the state's flagship skilling venues; PM-AJAY-funded training is expected to route through SSDM-affiliated providers per the central guidelines. (4) No Kerala government order publishing a state-approved trade list specifically under PM-AJAY was found on the pages accessed; SCDD's annual plan documents (scdd.kerala.gov.in/index.php/schemes/planning) are the closest official source and change yearly.

machine_usable_rule.reuse: Identical predicate as gia_funding_rules.json (Tamil Nadu pack): programme_type in [rpl, short_term, edp, long_term] AND sector in Annexure-I eligible list AND nsqf_compliant AND duration within type bounds AND cost <= MSDE Common Cost Norms AND placement >= 70%.

Tamil Nadu.scheme: PM-AJAY (Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana)
Tamil Nadu.component_analysed: Grants-in-Aid / 'Grant to States' component (the former Special Central Assistance to Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan, SCA-to-SCSP), which carries the scheme's skill-development mandate. PM-AJAY merged SCA-to-SCSP + PM-AGY (Adarsh Gram) + BJRCY (hostels) in 2021-22.
Tamil Nadu.prose_summary: The governing text is the consolidated SCA-to-SCSP guidelines (revised July 2020, carried into PM-AJAY) and the PM-AJAY Annual Action Plan circular. Findings: (1) There is NO trade-wise or QP-code whitelist anywhere in the guidelines. Eligibility is defined by programme TYPE and by an ILLUSTRATIVE sector/activity list (Annexure-I), not by QP code. (2) Four programme types are fundable: RPL/up-skilling (32-80 hours over up to 1 month); Short Term Courses focused on women and self-employment (normally 200-600 hours, up to 5 months, or as stipulated by the QP's NOS); EDP (normally 80 hours / 10 days, per MoRD norms); Long Term Courses (6 months and above, usually up to 1 year, as stipulated by the concerned board/regulator). (3) ALL training must comply with NSQF and MSDE Common Norms, including centre infrastructure, assessment and certification. (4) Training cost is capped by the MSDE Common Cost Norms (CCN) or NCVT guidelines; payments are milestone-based. The CCN tables themselves are a separate MSDE document and were not re-derived here. (5) At least 10% of released SCA must go to skill development; up to 30% to infrastructure; the skill programmes must deliver >=70% placement in wage or self-employment (for long-term courses, >=70% of the placed must be in wage employment). (6) Programmes are to be designed with NSDC skill-gap analysis and endorsed by the District Skilling Authority / State Skill Development Mission; executing agencies are SSDMs, their affiliated training providers, SSC-affiliated TIs, institutes on NSFDC's Appendix-I list, and others with a 70%-placement track record; long-term partners must have trained >=1,000 candidates over 3 years, in centres they own (no franchisee centres). (7) Beneficiary rules: SC persons below poverty line for individual benefits (PM-AJAY proposal moved individual funding to household income < Rs 2.5 lakh/yr); >=30% women; 5% of SCA for disabled persons' economic development. (8) Annexure-I's illustrative activity list covers: agriculture & soil conservation (incl. training of SC farmers, bee-keeping, sericulture); horticulture; minor irrigation; animal husbandry (milch cattle & dairy farming, poultry, goat/sheep, pigs & ducks); fisheries (fish production training, pisciculture, boats & nets, fishermen cooperatives); food processing; forestry/agro-forestry; handicrafts & handlooms; and 'Industry, Service and Business' - explicitly including leather units, carpentry/furniture, printing, brick-making, rubber, readymade garments, retail, gems & jewellery, electronics, bakery, beauty parlours, plumbing, automobile repair, IT/ITeS, media & entertainment, healthcare, and banking & financial services. (9) Tamil Nadu implementation: PM-AJAY is implemented by TAHDCO (Tamil Nadu Adi Dravidar Housing & Development Corporation) under the Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department; TAHDCO's PM-AJAY page describes income-generation assistance (subsidy 50% of project cost or Rs 50,000, whichever is lower - the revised PM-AJAY norm - for SC applicants with family income <= Rs 3 lakh) and TAHDCO funds skill courses (e.g., plastics processing at CIPET, textile diplomas, solar panel installation, CNC operation, cosmetology, hospitality, aviation reservations/cabin crew) through partner institutions. No Tamil Nadu state-published approved-trade list under PM-AJAY was found on the pages accessed; TAHDCO's skill catalogue on tahdco.com is the closest thing to a state trade list and changes with each tender.
